# Index

13 cases, newest first. Each line: title — kind, from to to; the share of the changed code AI produced, as the source states it (a contrast case, mostly rule-based, says so in its summary); how far the claims can be checked; the author's stake in the tools; the cost the source gives; a one-line summary.

Lessons drawn from the cases, by aspect: [lessons/index.md](lessons/index.md) (137 lessons on 16 pages). Before a migration: [checklist.md](checklist.md).

- [Bloomberg opens 2,333 migration PRs for Python packaging and C++ builds with a hybrid pipeline](cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md) — mixed, an in-house shared-environment Python packaging model; CppBuild, an in-house C++ build system to PyPackaging, an in-house per-package dependency model; CMake; AI share: part; evidence: shown-in-source; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. A rule-driven pipeline with Claude in bounded steps opened 2,333 packaging and build PRs; 729 were merged, and most got no decision from their owners.
- [GitHub moves its Copilot agent runtime from TypeScript to Rust using agents](cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md) — language, TypeScript on Node.js and V8 to Rust (native library with a C ABI); AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$120,000 for ~136.3 billion tokens (engineer time not priced). One engineer steered agent fleets to port about 430,000 lines of TypeScript to Rust in place, one component per PR, over 14.5 weeks.
- [Shopify rebuilds its React Native mobile apps natively for iOS and Android](cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md) — language, React Native apps (Shop first; Shopify, Point of Sale, Inbox to follow) to native iOS (Swift, SwiftUI) and Android (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) apps; AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Agents port Shopify's React Native apps to native iOS and Android code through gated checkpoints; one-shot ports failed, and the Shop app shipped in 12 weeks.
- [Intel's IDEAS harness ports the libgit2 command-line client in C to safe Rust](cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md) — language, C (libgit2 command-line client) to safe Rust (no unsafe code); AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$0.55 per symbol for translation (total unstated), plus ~$6.5 for repair. An LLM harness turned 112K lines of C into safe Rust that compiled but crashed; 8 person-hours guiding an agent got git blame working.
- [Asana finishes its Enzyme to React Testing Library move with Codex agents in two weeks](cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (frontend React tests) to React Testing Library; AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$11,000 model usage plus ~$1,000 infrastructure. Up to 4 Codex agents on a 5-sentence prompt removed Enzyme in about 1.5 weeks of engineering time for about $12K; stale docs and slow lint got in the way.
- [Bun moves its JavaScript runtime off Zig onto Rust with Claude agents in 11 days](cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md) — language, Zig (Bun runtime, bundler, package manager, test runner) to Rust (about 100 crates); AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$165,000 at API list prices for the tokens used before merge (690 million output tokens, 5.9 billion fresh input tokens, 72 billion cached input tokens). One engineer ran about 50 Claude Code workflows, up to 64 agents at once, to port 535K lines of Zig to Rust in 11 days; 19 known regressions, all fixed.
- [1Password uses AI agents to refactor its Go monolith and begin a service extraction](cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md) — architecture, Go monolith (B5), database transactions opened with MustBegin (panics on failure) to separately owned services; transaction calls that return errors; AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Agents rewrote over 3,000 panicking transaction calls from a tight spec, but stumbled on a service extraction's ordering and invariants.
- [Uber moves 75K test classes off JUnit 4 onto JUnit 5 with OpenRewrite; an AI attempt failed](cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md) — test-framework, Java tests on JUnit 4 in a Bazel monorepo to Java tests on JUnit 5 (Jupiter engine on the JUnit Platform); AI share: little; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Contrast case. Rule-based OpenRewrite recipes moved over 75,000 Java test classes onto JUnit 5; a generative-AI attempt failed and AI only helped debug.
- [Spotify runs fleet-wide migrations with its Honk background coding agent](cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md) — mixed, many (for example Java AutoValue classes, old Scio versions, deprecated datasets) to many (for example Java records, the newest Scio, new dataset versions); AI share: most; evidence: assertion-only; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. Spotify put a coding agent inside its fleet migration tooling; verifiers and an LLM judge gate each PR, and over 1,500 agent PRs were merged.
- [Google widens int32 IDs to int64 in 39 migrations with an LLM pipeline](cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md) — data, int32 ID fields in protocol buffer schemas and the code using them (Java, C++, Dart and others) to int64 ID fields; AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. A nightly pipeline of code search, rule-based sorting, an internal Gemini model and staged checks drafted 74.45% of 595 code changes in 39 ID migrations.
- [Airbnb moves 3.5K React test files off Enzyme onto React Testing Library](cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (React component tests) to React Testing Library; AI share: most; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. An LLM pipeline with per-file validation steps and retries migrated 97% of about 3,500 React test files; people finished the rest by hand.
- [Zalando moves partner apps from one in-house UI component library to another with GPT-4o](cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md) — framework, in-house UI component library (React) to another in-house UI component library (React); AI share: part; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: under $40 per repository in GPT-4o API fees (estimate). A Python tool fed GPT-4o hand-checked mappings and examples per component group; about 90% of migrated lines were right, and one bad change reached production.
- [Slack pairs a syntax-tree codemod with Claude 2.1 to help move 15K Enzyme tests to React Testing Library](cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (React unit and integration tests) to React Testing Library; AI share: unstated; evidence: shown-in-source; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Codemod alone 45% (evaluation files), Claude 2.1 alone 40-60% (base not given), both 80% of code in 9 checked files; 22% of tests passed over 338 files.
